messages.content: You check each debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words given to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge one side by the other side's words.

You are the closing enforcer. A debater's closing round may not contradict what the same debater stated in its earlier rounds. Below are one debater's four rounds.
Read its closing round against its earlier rounds. List every closing sentence that cannot be true together with an earlier sentence, and answer every candidate listed.
A contradiction is two statements that cannot both be true. Two sentences of the same closing round that cannot both be true are also a contradiction: quote the first as EARLIER [<round 4>] and the second as CLOSING [<round 4>]. A closing sentence that asserts again, as the debater's own, what it withdrew, dropped, narrowed or gave up in an earlier round IS a contradiction. A closing sentence that restores the wider wording or the ground of a claim the debater narrowed or gave up in an earlier round ("I narrow", "I withdraw", "I do not rest") asserts it again; check the close against every one listed under EARLIER NARROWINGS.
It is NOT a contradiction when the closing sentence: grants, concedes, narrows or withdraws something; states or quotes the other side's position; answers a press with a further reason the earlier sentence leaves room for; differs only in wording; or differs only by a reference: it ties its point to a verse whose words, as the debater's own rounds quote them, do not give that point (a wrong reference, or one grouped with the verse that does give it). Read such a sentence with that reference set aside; if its point then agrees with the earlier sentence, it is not a contradiction. A sentence whose point itself cannot be true with the earlier sentence is still a contradiction, whatever its references.
Read a withdrawal by its meaning, not its words: a closing sentence that says again in other words what the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or gave up, or rests its reason on it, asserts it again. "Differs only in wording" clears two sentences that make the same claim; it never clears a closing sentence that makes again a claim the debater withdrew. A closing sentence that states only what the debater kept, or rests the same conclusion on other rows, does not assert it again. When the earlier sentence rests no weight on a verse or row, a closing sentence that uses that verse or row as a footing for the same link or the same purpose asserts it again.
Read each candidate's closing sentence together with the rows of its CLOSING BLOCK: a closing sentence that draws its point from a row ("So", "Therefore", "Thus") asserts what that row says, so if the earlier sentence withdrew, dropped or rested nothing on that row, the close asserts it again.
Quote both sentences word for word and name the link: the link whose closing block holds the sentence, else the link the earlier sentence supports.
Reply with one line per contradiction and per candidate, and nothing else:
CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: <candidate id or NEW> -- <DEFENDER|CHALLENGER> -- LINK <n> -- CONFIRMED | NOT A CONTRADICTION -- EARLIER [<round>] "<words>" -- CLOSING [<round 4>] "<words>" -- <one sentence: why both cannot be true, or why they can>
If you find none and there is no candidate, reply: CLOSE-CONTRADICTION: NONE

CANDIDATES ALREADY NAMED (answer each one by its id):

EARLIER NARROWINGS (this side's own, rounds 1 to 3, listed by the code; the narrowing sentence is marked >> <<; check the close against each, and write NEW for a contradiction you find):

######## THE DEFENDER ########
The defender's links: D1 = LINK 1, D2 = LINK 2, D3 = LINK 3, D4 = LINK 4, D5 = LINK 5 (its DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1]). Its closing round is [CR4].

=== [CR1] ===
DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

Christ had a biological father. The father is named, and the seed is required to come out of a man's body.

The promise requires seed out of a man's body, according to the flesh [L1] [L3] [L4].

2 Samuel 7:12 says: "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom." [L1]

Its "thy seed" is zera' (H2233) meaning seed, posterity, fruit [L2]. Its "out of thy bowels" names the man's own body as the place the seed proceeds from [L4 footed on L1+L2].

Psalm 132:11 says: "The LORD hath sworn [in] truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." [L1] Its "body" carries the margin Heb. belly [L1 margin].

1 Kings 8:19 says: "Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name." [L1] [L3]

Genesis 35:11 says: "And God said unto him, I [am] God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;" [L1] [L3]

Romans 1:3 says: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" [L1] Its "seed" is sperma (G4690) meaning seed, offspring, something sown including the male sperm [L2].

Acts 2:30 says: "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;" [L1] [L3] Its "loins" is the loins-word of Hebrews 7:10, osphys (G3751) meaning the loin, procreative power [L2].

Hebrews 7:14 says: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood." [L1] [L3] 2 Timothy 2:8 says: "Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel:" [L1] [L3]

So a real seed proceeding out of the body, according to the flesh, evident, cannot stand with no man [L4 footed on L1 2 Samuel 7:12 + Romans 1:3 and L2 zera' meaning seed + sperma meaning seed and L3 Acts 2:30 + Hebrews 7:14].

The father is named in four registers, and the one man the text names is Joseph, of the house of David [L1] [L3] [L4].

Mary herself says in Luke 2:48: "And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." [L1]

The narrator names in Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him." [L1] And in Luke 2:41: "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover." [L1] [L3] And in Luke 2:27: "And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law," [L1] [L3]

The town says in Luke 4:22: "And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph's son?" [L1] And in John 6:42: "And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" [L1] [L3] A disciple says in John 1:45: "Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." [L1] [L3]

The angel says in Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" [L1 whole with its margin] Its "conceived" is gennao (G1080) meaning to procreate, properly of the father, by extension of the mother [L2].

Joseph is "of the house of David" in Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary." [L1] And in Luke 2:4: "And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" [L1] [L3] The throne given is "the throne of his father David" in Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:" [L1] [L3]

Therefore the named father is Joseph, thou son of David [L4 footed on L1 Luke 2:48 + Matthew 1:20 and L2 gennao meaning to procreate of the father and L3 Luke 2:33 + John 6:42].

Reckoning is by the house of the fathers, and the register was struck for the wife's house [L1] [L2] [L3] [L4].

Numbers 1:2 says: "Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls;" [L1] Numbers 1:18 says: "And they assembled all the congregation together on the first [day] of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls." [L1] [L3]

"By the house of their fathers" is le-veit avotam: bayith (H1004) meaning house, family, and ab (H1) meaning father [L2].

Ezra 2:59 says: "And these [were] they which went up from Telmelah, Telharsa, Cherub, Addan, [and] Immer: but they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [Addan: also called, Addon] [seed: or, pedigree]" [L1 with its margin] Ezra 2:61 says: "And of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Koz, the children of Barzillai; which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name:" [L1] Ezra 2:62 says: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood. [were they...: Heb. they were polluted from the priesthood]" [L1] [L3] It gives its own cause, they were not found, therefore as polluted put from the priesthood; it does not say a name taken through a wife's house was refused [L4 footed on L1 Ezra 2:62 + L3 Ezra 2:59].

Ruth 4:10 says: "Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye [are] witnesses this day." [L1] [L3]

No row gives Mary's lineage [L4 footed on L1 Luke 1:5 + Luke 1:36 and L3 Numbers 1:2]. Luke 1:5 gives Elisabeth "of the daughters of Aaron" [L1]. Luke 1:36 calls Elisabeth Mary's cousin, in the KJV "thy cousin Elisabeth" [L1]: "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren." [L1] Luke 3:23 names no female name: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli," [L1]. Its "as was supposed" is hōs (G5613) meaning as, like as, and enomizeto, from nomizo (G3543) meaning to deem, to suppose, to be wont, by custom [L2]; the same form is at Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made" [L3], so the word carries no verdict of its own.

"Of the Holy Ghost" is covenant-origin, not paternity; "Son of God" is covenant and resurrection title, not biology [L1] [L2] [L3] [L4].

Matthew 1:18 says: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." [L1] Read whole with Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." [L1] [L3] Its "just" is dikaios (G1342) meaning equitable, innocent, just [L2], coordinate with "not willing," not set against it.

The angel's "for" grounds the command to take her: the child in her is holy, the Anointed [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:20 + Matthew 1:21 and L3 Luke 2:11]. Matthew 1:21 says: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]" [L1] [L3] Luke 2:11 says at his birth: "For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord." [L1] [L3] "Christ" is Christos (G5547) meaning anointed [L2].

Luke 1:35 says: "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L1] Its "shall come upon" is eperchomai (G1904) meaning to come upon [L2]. Acts 1:8 says: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth. [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]" [L1] [L3] That is power for witness, not a begetting. Its "shall overshadow" is episkiazo (G1982) meaning to overshadow, to cast shade upon [L2]. Matthew 17:5 says: "While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him." [L1] [L3] Mark 9:7 and Luke 9:34 give the same cloud [L3]. Luke 9:34 says: "While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud." [L1] Acts 5:15 gives the same word of Peter's shadow [L3]: "Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid [them] on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them. [into...: or, in every street]" [L1]. Neither row denotes begetting at any row [L4 footed on L1 Luke 1:35 + Acts 1:8 and L2 eperchomai meaning to come upon + episkiazo meaning to overshadow and L3 Matthew 17:5 + Acts 5:15].

The "therefore" in Luke 1:35 is dio kai meaning therefore also [L2]. It connects back to Luke 1:32, not forward to biology [L4 footed on L1 Luke 1:32 + Luke 1:35 and L3 2 Samuel 7:14]. Luke 1:32 gives the title with the throne before Mary asks in Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L1]. Its "know" is present active, her state when spoken, not a vow [L4 footed on L1 Luke 1:34 and L2 ginosko meaning to know and L3 Matthew 1:25].

"Son of God" is given to Solomon while Solomon had a father [L1] [L3]. 2 Samuel 7:14 says: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:" [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6 says: "And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." [L1] [L3] In one verse the son David begat and the covenant title God gave him. Psalm 2:7 says: "I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee. [the decree: or, for a decree]" [L1] Quoted at three occasions: Acts 13:33: "God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee." [L1] [L3]; Hebrews 5:5 and Hebrews 1:5: "For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?" [L1] [L3]. Romans 1:4 says: "And declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]" [L1] [L3] Luke 1:35 says "shall be CALLED the Son of God" [L1].

He was made like his brethren, in all things, and mixing kinds is forbidden [L1] [L2] [L3] [L4].

Hebrews 2:14 says: "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;" [L1] Hebrews 2:16 says: "For verily he took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]" [L1 with its margin] Hebrews 2:17 says: "Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things [pertaining] to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people." [L1] [L3] John 1:14 says: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth." [L1] [L3]

Leviticus 19:19 says: "Ye shall keep my statutes. Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender with a diverse kind: thou shalt not sow thy field with mingled seed: neither shall a garment mingled of linen and woollen come upon thee." [L1] Its "diverse kind" and "mingled" is kilayim (H3610) meaning two heterogeneities, divers seeds, mingled [L2]; its "gender" is raba (H7250) meaning to lie down in copulation, to gender [L2].

Genesis 1:11 says: "And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, [and] the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed [is] in itself, upon the earth: and it was so. [grass: Heb. tender grass]" [L1] 1 Corinthians 15:38 says: "But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body." [L1] [L3] 1 Corinthians 15:39 says: "All flesh [is] not the same flesh: but [there is] one [kind of] flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, [and] another of birds." [L1] [L3]

John 3:6 is carried as support: that which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit [L3]. So to read "of the Holy Ghost" as the Holy Ghost begetting flesh joins two kinds, which God's own statute forbids [L4 footed on L1 Leviticus 19:19 + Hebrews 2:14 and L2 kilayim meaning mingled + raba meaning to gender and L3 John 3:6 + 1 Corinthians 15:39].

The union is stated by the rows: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal [L1] [L3] [L4].

Genesis 4:1 gives the canon's stated means: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]" [L1] Its "knew" is yada (H3045) meaning to know [L2].

Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19) [L1]; "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) [L1] [L3]. Matthew 1:24 says: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:" [L1] Matthew 1:25 says: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L1] [L3]

Matthew 1:18's "before they came together" is answered by Matthew 1:24's "took unto him his wife," the coming under one roof; the union's word is "knew" in Matthew 1:25 [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:18 + Matthew 1:24 + Matthew 1:25 and L2 synerchomai (G4905) meaning to convene, to come together, to cohabit and L3 Genesis 4:1]. The finding with child is told before the taking; the not-knowing is told after it. The withholding runs from the taking to the birth, and the begetting stands before it, within the espousal [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:18 + Matthew 1:24 + Matthew 1:25 and L3 Genesis 4:1 + Ruth 4:13 "when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception"].

Joseph's intent in Matthew 1:19 is read by Mark 7:7: "Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching [for] doctrines the commandments of men," [L1] Mark 7:8: "For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men," [L1] [L3] Mark 7:9: "Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition." [L1] [L3] And Colossians 2:8 after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ [L3]. The scorn is tradition's, not law's; the child is Joseph's and he knew it [L4 footed on L1 Matthew 1:19 + Matthew 1:20 and L3 Mark 7:8 + Genesis 4:1].

DECLARED CHAIN
D1: The promised seed must proceed out of a man's bowels/loins/body according to the flesh -- exhibits 2 Samuel 7:12 [L1] + zera' (H2233) meaning seed [L2] + Romans 1:3 which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh [L3], therefore seed out of a man's body [L4].
D2: The father is named as Joseph, thou son of David -- exhibits Matthew 1:20 Joseph, thou son of David ... Mary thy wife [L1] + gennao (G1080) meaning to procreate of the father [L2] + Luke 2:48 behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing and John 6:42 son of Joseph [L3], therefore Joseph is the named Davidic father [L4].
D3: Reckoning is by the house of the fathers, not through the mother alone -- exhibits Numbers 1:2 by the house of their fathers [L1] + ab (H1) meaning father [L2] + Ezra 2:59-62 could not shew their father's house ... as polluted, put from the priesthood [L3], therefore lineage runs through the father's house [L4].
D4: Of the Holy Ghost and Son of God are covenant/anointing markers, and the angel's verbs are presence and power -- exhibits Matthew 1:20 that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost with Joseph, thou son of David [L1] + ek (G1537) meaning from, out ... denoting origin [L2] + Luke 1:32 throne of his father David + Acts 1:8 after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you + Matthew 17:5 overshadowed + Romans 1:4 declared Son of God by resurrection + Acts 13:33 this day have I begotten thee at the resurrection [L3], therefore no begetting of flesh by the Spirit [L4].
D5: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins -- exhibits Matthew 1:19 Joseph her husband + Matthew 1:20 Mary thy wife + Matthew 1:25 knew her not till [L1] + yada (H3045) meaning to know in Genesis 4:1 Adam knew Eve his wife and she conceived [L2+L3], therefore Jesus had a biological father, Joseph [L4].

=== [CR2] ===
DEFENDER (record's reading) -- ROUND 2, RESPONSE

The chain stands. The seed must come out of a man's body, the father is named, reckoning runs by the fathers, the Spirit's part is covenant and anointing, and the union is in the espousal.

**Premise 1 answered -- Matthew 1:18 before they came together, Matthew 1:20 of the Holy Ghost, Matthew 1:16 of whom**

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L1] Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:"
[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

It fits the link. Matthew 1:18 dates the finding. Matthew 1:24 sets what came together, took unto him his wife, her coming into his house. Matthew 1:25 sets the union's word, knew, and bounds the withholding from the taking to the birth. [L2] synerchomai (G4905) in Matthew 1:18: "to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally):--accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort." [L2] gennao (G1080) in Matthew 1:20 margin Gr. begotten: "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate." [L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]" [L3] Ruth 4:13: "So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bare a son."

[L4] footed on [L1] Matthew 1:19 Joseph her husband + Matthew 1:20 Mary thy wife + Matthew 1:25 till and [L3] Genesis 4:1 knew + conceived and Ruth 4:13 went in + LORD gave conception: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. The finding before the taking in Matthew 1:18, the taking in Matthew 1:24, and the not-knowing after it in Matthew 1:25 hold one order. Luke 2:5: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. [taxed: or, enrolled]" [L1] names her as his espoused wife on the journey, and Matthew 1:24 names her taken as wife. It fits the link.

Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." [L1] is non-narration. It does not beget, it births. [L3] Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;" [L3] Acts 2:30: "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;" Precept upon precept, the rest of the witnesses fill what that one verse leaves quiet. It fits D1 and D5.

**Premise 2 answered -- Matthew 1:19 just, Matthew 1:20 for**

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] dikaios (G1342): "from dike; equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively):--just, meet, right(-eous)." [L2] thelo (G2309) in not willing carries choose, wish, be inclined to. The two are coordinate joined by kai, one intent stated from two angles.

[L1] Matthew 1:20 whole row above names in the same breath "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife" with "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" The for grounds the command to take her: the child in her is holy, the Anointed. [L3] Matthew 1:21: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]" [L3] Luke 2:11: "For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord." [L2] Christos (G5547): "from chrio; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus:--Christ."

[L1] Mark 7:7: "Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching [for] doctrines the commandments of men." [L1] Mark 7:8: "For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, [as] the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do." [L1] Mark 7:9: "And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition. [reject: or, frustrate]" [L3] Colossians 2:8: "Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ. [rudiments: or, elements] [make a prey: or, seduce you, or, lead you astray]"
[L4] footed on [L1] Matthew 1:19 being a just man and not willing + Matthew 1:20 Joseph her husband's taking and [L3] Mark 7:8 laying aside the commandment of God ye hold the tradition of men: Joseph's unwillingness to make her a publick example IS his righteousness toward Mary his wife, against the scorn of men's tradition, and the child is his and he knew it. It fits D5.

**Premise 3 answered -- Luke 1:34 know not, Luke 1:35 come upon and overshadow therefore, Luke 1:37 impossible**

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
